# Test Fixtures

## Synthetic screenshots

Generated by `tests/fixtures/generate_screenshots.py`. Run once after install:

```bash
python -m tests.fixtures.generate_screenshots
```

This produces four fixtures in `tests/fixtures/screenshots/`:

| File | Content | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `signboard_roastery.png` | Bold cafe name + tagline + location | Easy OCR test |
| `menu_niloufer.png` | Cafe name + menu items with prices | Multi-line OCR test |
| `address_driftwood.png` | Name + full address + phone | Full-context test |
| `low_signal.png` | Only generic words like "Welcome" | Low-confidence test |

These are synthetic and rendered with PIL, so PaddleOCR should hit them with very high confidence. They verify the **wiring**, not real-world accuracy.

## Real screenshots (optional)

To test PaddleOCR on real-world Reels/video screenshots:

1. Drop files into `tests/fixtures/screenshots/real/`
2. Add a manifest JSON describing expected text and place name
3. Run `RUN_REAL_OCR=1 pytest tests/test_real_ocr.py` (you'll need to write this test, not included by default since it requires a PaddleOCR install)

## Why no real screenshots are committed

Real cafe screenshots may contain identifiable people, copyrighted signage, or watermarks from Instagram/YouTube. Synthetic fixtures sidestep all of that and keep the repo small and license-clean.
